Thousands of tests were conducted on integrated circuits of various types and manufacturers to determine their susceptibility to microwave signals.
The minimum power levels that caused interference or damage in TTL, CMOS, op amps, voltage regulators, comparators, and line drivers/receivers were measured and presented in graphs.
Interference effects were observed to decrease with increasing frequency of the interfering signal.
Modulation of the interfering RF signal resulted in modulation of the interference effect seen in the circuit outputs.
Permanent damage to integrated circuits can occur when the RF power level is high enough to cause irreversible thermal effects.
The modeling techniques in Chapter 5 can be used to analyze interference effects in ICs not specifically tested, including worst-case analyses.
A worst-case approach is recommended to determine the maximum RF power picked up by system cables from the environment.
The hardening requirement is defined as the ratio of the maximum expected pickup level to the minimum component susceptibility level.
If the hardening requirement is less than 0 dB, no additional hardening is needed, but if it exceeds 0 dB, hardening measures must be implemented.
Hardening measures below 30 dB can be implemented directly, but above 30 dB, a more detailed vulnerability analysis is recommended.
The handbook focuses on the 100 MHz to 40 GHz frequency range, with the upper limit of practical concern being closer to 10 GHz.
Theoretical and practical considerations suggest the worst-case interference problems are adequately covered in the 100 MHz to 40 GHz range.

The proposed system hardening approach involves five key steps: environment specification, cable pickup assessment, component susceptibility determination, vulnerability assessment, and hardening implementation.

The handbook is intended to provide the information needed to estimate the susceptibility of circuits containing ICs to RF energy and to approach the hardening task required for high-power RF environments.
The handbook is the final version that incorporates feedback from previous drafts and is expected to be a valuable resource for many years.
